### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via hostSignInHandoff (symbol, a field of interface AuthPluginOptions; a field of interface SignInPathHostView; a field of interface SignInPathWiring))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4edb61449bcef5204cf5e2a81348695f9b4e9a61` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c5ece634dae8deab5bcc1e6a79b23eba86b4834f` — the merge of head `88aff6fe7e605abaf420fd3e7343211dc2403ce1` into base `4edb61449bcef5204cf5e2a81348695f9b4e9a61`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c5ece634dae8deab5bcc1e6a79b23eba86b4834f && git checkout c5ece634dae8deab5bcc1e6a79b23eba86b4834f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4edb61449bcef5204cf5e2a81348695f9b4e9a61 88aff6fe7e605abaf420fd3e7343211dc2403ce1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4edb61449bcef5204cf5e2a81348695f9b4e9a61 && git merge --no-ff 88aff6fe7e605abaf420fd3e7343211dc2403ce1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4edb61449bcef5204cf5e2a81348695f9b4e9a61
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4edb61449bcef5204cf5e2a81348695f9b4e9a61` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `88aff6fe7e605abaf420fd3e7343211dc2403ce1`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #20861 (body and all four comments: triage 5912860738, claim 5913893583, dev report 5914902012, accept 5914937082), PR #20893 (body, file list, and the net diff at the head against merge-base `9905e61ca2fddb43d266c23cdb12ced5019c1a74`), and the head's check-runs. Read-only throughout: git objects at the head, no worktree, no build, no test, no gate re-run.

Check-runs on the head, latest per name, read at 2026-09-30T16:08Z: 30 success, 2 skipped (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failure, and 2 still in progress at this reading: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Type Check · workspace`. Of the required contexts, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green; the lint job and the type-check workspace leg were still running, so the lint context and the type-check rollup had not been posted. Landing still waits on those two; this record judges the contract, not the queue.

### ① Derived judgments

Net diff: 5 files, +241 / −5, every path on the claim's file surface; no `packages/spec` path, no governed path, no cloud change. `main` has moved 7 commits / 119 files past the merge-base at this reading and none of them touches `packages/plugins/plugin-auth`, the docs page or the changeset path, so the no-merge decision holds and CI's merge ref carries the combined tree.

1. **`AuthPluginOptions.hostSignInHandoff?: boolean` — public, widening — right.** The interface is re-exported from the `.` entry (`export * from './auth-plugin.js'`), so the option is a published host surface. It joins the existing host-wiring idiom (`manifestDatasource`, `databaseHooks`, `membershipPolicy`) rather than the spec `AuthConfig`; a spec key would make the fact authorable from metadata, and a metadata author cannot know which routes the host mounts, which is exactly triage's ⛔ on inference. The claim's spec-lane stop condition therefore did not fire, correctly.
2. **The option's reach — right, and the changeset's "only reader" sentence is true.** Measured at the head: the only non-declaration reads are `auth-plugin.ts:1082` (the `kernel:ready` hook handing `this.options` to the gate) and the gate module. `this.options` is written once, in the constructor; `applyConfigPatch` patches the manager's config, not the plugin's options, so no settings-console value reaches the gate. The option is also spread into the manager's `authConfig`, but nothing in `auth-manager.ts` walks config keys generically, spreads `this.config` into `betterAuth()`, or exposes it; `getPublicConfig()` builds every field explicitly. So "no env var, no setting, no public-config change" is true of the delivered behaviour, and the pin comparing the live manager's `getPublicConfig()` with and without the declaration holds it.
3. **`SignInPathWiring` gains a required member `hostSignInHandoff: boolean` — right, and internal.** The gate module is not re-exported from `src/index.ts` (`auth-plugin.ts` only imports it), so the narrowing never reaches the published `.d.ts`. The only literal constructors at the head are `probeSignInPathWiring` and the suite's `NOTHING_WIRED`; the #14353 suite constructs no wiring literal and is unedited.
4. **`probeSignInPathWiring` fourth parameter `host?: SignInPathHostView` — right.** Optional, structural, and read with strict equality to `true` only (the string `'true'`, `1`, `'yes'` and `null` all read as not declared, pinned). A declared handoff short-circuits the `sys_sso_provider` read exactly as `ssoOnlyMode` and `socialSignIn` already do: one reason per boot, by #15074's design. The handoff is last in `resolveDelegatedSignInPath`, so a deployment that also declares SSO-only names SSO-only, the more specific fact.
5. **The report's behaviour — right.** `resolveNoSignInAccountReport` answers `null` on the declared fact; `reportIfNoSignInAccountExists` records the shape at `debug` under `no_sign_in_account_at_boot` with a reason string naming `hostSignInHandoff`; the `error` text is unchanged and does not mention the option (the only occurrences in the gate module are the module doc, the interface members, the probe and the reason string). A deployment that does not declare it reports exactly as before, held by the CONTROL pin.
6. **The docs page, sentence by sentence — every added sentence is true of the delivered behaviour.** "SSO-only mode (`OS_AUTH_SSO_ONLY` or `ssoOnlyMode`)": `resolveSsoOnly()` reads that env var, then the config key, and advertises it as `features.ssoEnforced`, which the gate reads. "a configured social or OIDC provider": `getPublicConfig()` pushes every social provider whose `enabled` is not `false` and every `oidcProviders` entry into `socialProviders`, which the gate reads as `socialSignIn`. "enterprise SSO with at least one registered identity provider": `features.sso` plus one `sys_sso_provider` row. "under the same token and naming the reason": the `debug` line carries the token and the reason. "A deployment with none of these still reports at error": true of the default logger (the module's `warn` fallback for a sink without `error` predates this PR, and the page already describes the default). The closing warning is accurate: set without a route, the option drops the report to `debug`. The page is hand-written (not `references/`) and pre-existing, so no `meta.json` change is owed; `Build Docs` and `Check Documentation Links` are green.
7. **The PR's "For the cloud follow-up" line — right as stated.** The one declaration cloud must make is `hostSignInHandoff: true` where it constructs `AuthPlugin`; nothing else in this repo has to move for it.
8. **No route, env var, spec schema, ADR anchor or generated artifact is touched — right.** No ADR in `docs/adr/` and no `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry names this gate, so no decision is reversed and none needs anchoring; no `OS_` var is introduced; no query-parameter set is owed.

One observation, not a finding: the hook hands the whole `this.options` object (secret included) into `probeSignInPathWiring` under the structural view. The gate reads one boolean and never logs the object, so nothing leaks; a one-field projection would be narrower, but the module doc states the pass-through deliberately.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/20861-host-sign-in-handoff.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: minor`, carrying `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and the one-line declaration a host writes. PR body line 2: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Right on both counts: the diff publishes one new optional member on an exported interface (`dist/index.d.ts` through the `.` entry), which is a widening of the public options surface, so `yes` is owed and `minor` is the floor. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker and no migration text are owed, and `skip-changeset` would have been wrong. `Check Changeset` is green. The changeset's first line reads `feat(plugin-auth)` while the PR title reads `fix(plugin-auth)`; no gate reads the prefix, `feat` matches the `minor` level and `fix` matches the card's `bug` label, so this is cosmetic and not held against the record.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions: []`** — none raised, and none owed: triage fully specified the direction.
- **Out-of-scope finding: the walled-owner neighbour (`warnIfWalledOwnerCannotVerify`) reads `hasFederatedSignIn` from `getPublicConfig()` alone, not from `hostSignInHandoff`.** Answered: correctly noted, not filed. It is #15074's pinned design (the independence pins at `boot-sign-in-reachability.test.ts:762` and `:783` hold the two reports apart); whether it bites on a hidden-button hosted kernel depends on four preconditions this repo cannot measure (walled posture, declared owner, no transport, no federated path); and if it does, the symptom is a `warn` under its own token, not the ERROR this card was filed for. The carrier is right: the cloud follow-up card's rebuild log. A hit there is its own card with its own fix shape.
- **Dev note (1): `main` moved during the run, no merge made.** Answered: verified at this reading against the current `origin/main` (7 commits, 119 files since the merge-base; none under `packages/plugins/plugin-auth`, the docs page or the changeset), so the same-day-churn clause was applied correctly.
- **Dev note (2): attribution.** Answered: both commits on the branch carry the model-free `Claude-Session` and co-author trailer pair the pre-push hook requires, and the PR body carries the session-URL footer; the harness reminder yields to AGENTS.md here, as it should.
- **Dev note (3): the `size/m` label was set by another actor and left alone.** Answered: right; state a seat did not set is not the seat's to correct.
- **The claim's spec-lane stop condition** (the fact having to be a spec-declared config key): did not fire, rightly, per ① item 1.
- **Cross-repository follow-up** (triage: a cloud card `Blocked-by:` this one): not a dev flag; the accept comment assigns it to the landing seat, and the PR body carries the one line that card needs. Nothing for this record to escalate.
